cards.summary: Older build of Dip to Black: the outgoing clip fades to black, then the incoming clip fades up from black, with linear ramps (gallery: steady darkening, full black at the cut). The current eased 'Dip to Black' replaces it.
use_for: chapter or act break in a documentary
after a heavy or sombre line in a news explainer
fade out at the end of a reel or film (single-sided)
trailer beat before a title card
Chapter or act break in a documentary
Fade out at the very end of a video
Black beat between trailer title cards (pair with a boom)
Respectful pause after a tragedy or tribute segment

too many in one piece: kills pace
Mid-sentence under continuous VO: reads as an ending
Overuse in a reel kills pace
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Dip to Black (non-legacy). After Effects: a black Solid above both layers with Opacity 0->100 into the cut and 100->0 after it (or fade each layer's Opacity over a black background).
cards.scripting: Apply by the exact name including ' (Legacy)'. The QE list contains this name twice (both entries share this card); both behave the same. cards.name: Inset
cards.summary: The incoming clip is revealed in a hard-edged rectangle that starts in the top-left corner and grows diagonally until it fills the frame. It is a wipe: the incoming image is cropped, not scaled (gallery shows subjects at their full-frame positions inside the growing box).
use_for: deliberately retro / 90s TV parody segment in a satire reel
revealing a document or screenshot from a corner in an explainer
comic 'cut to' gag
avoid: serious documentaries: reads as cheap slideshow
the hard edge looks dated at normal speed in trailers
cards.equivalent: After Effects: a rectangle mask on the incoming layer whose size animates from a corner to full frame (or Linear Wipe at 45 degrees for a softer variant); a scale-from-corner with Transform is the moving-picture version.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (269.52-270.52 s) with no error. Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) confirms the default: box grows from the top-left corner, incoming image unscaled. Corner choice and border are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec, so the bridge always gets top-left. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: Hard-edged box of B grows from the top-left corner (small at -0.3 s, ~half frame at the cut, most of frame at +0.3 s) and shows B cropped at its full-frame positions, not scaled.

cards.name: Morph Cut
cards.summary: Hides a jump cut inside a talking-head shot by face tracking and optical-flow interpolation between the last frame before the cut and the first frame after it, so the speaker appears to talk continuously.
use_for: removing ums, pauses or a cut sentence in a locked-off interview
tightening a politician's soundbite without a visible jump
AI-education talking-head videos with one static camera
avoid: between different shots or camera moves: produces melting warps
big head turns, hands crossing the face or long gaps: visible morphing artefacts
durations over ~0.5 s
objects that move between the two halves of the jump (a locked-off shot with things moving through it): measured, they tear into smeared ghost copies at the cut
cards.feel: invisible when it works, uncanny when it fails
cards.equivalent: No one-click equivalent in After Effects; approximate with Timewarp (Method: Pixel Motion) over a pre-comp of both sides of the cut, or hide the jump with a punch-in / B-roll cutaway.
cards.scripting: Centred only, needs handles on both clips from the same static shot. Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (273.52-274.52 s) with no error; on the gallery's two DIFFERENT shots it rendered a smeared, torn double exposure with blocky streaks, which is exactly the failure case, so never use it as a generic transition. For real use set 0.2-0.5 s on a jump cut inside one interview clip. Measured 2026-10-14 (live wave 3) on a synthetic face plate with a 1.2 s jump and a 0.6 s Morph Cut: the largest frame-to-frame change across the cut was 0.24 (the plate's own motion is 0.22-0.24) against 0.75 for the same jump as a hard cut, and the frames at the cut show one clean face, no double exposure; the same Morph Cut on a plate whose objects move between the two halves tore them into smeared ghost shapes. Premiere analyses the clip in the background after it is applied ('Analyzing in background' banner); a scripted export started before analysis completes carries the banner (measured: still there 150 s after the build, gone at 159 s on the rerun), so poll Sequence.isDoneAnalyzingForVideoEffects() or export again until no frame shows it.

verified.note: On its real job (a jump inside one static face shot) the cut is invisible: no frame-change spike (0.24 vs 0.75 for the hard cut) and one clean face at the cut; on a plate with moving objects the cut frame shows torn ghost shapes, the failure the card warns about.

previous.why: judged on its real use case in the live wave 3 two-track test (work/pve_live/wave3/two_track.json); the old pass showed only the failure case on two different shots
previous.note: On two different shots it renders the documented failure: a smeared, torn, washed-out double exposure with blocky vertical streaks, not a seamless join.

cards.name: Non-Additive Dissolve
cards.summary: A luminance-comparison dissolve: per pixel it shows whichever clip is brighter, with hard edges instead of a soft mix. The bright areas of the incoming clip (sky, lights, pale surfaces) punch through the outgoing clip's darker areas from the first frames, the two images hold as a patchy, posterised double exposure for most of the duration, and the incoming clip's dark areas only take over at the end.
use_for: stylised double-exposure beat in a music-driven montage or trailer
transitioning into a bright title card or logo on black (only the bright graphic shows through)
night city, fire or stage-light footage where the lights should bleed through
graphic portrait-into-bright-landscape moment in a reel
avoid: faces and skin: the hard-edged blotches look like compression damage
two clips of similar brightness: a noisy patchwork for the whole duration (seen in the gallery)
news and documentary transitions: reads as a render error, use Cross Dissolve or Film Dissolve
cards.equivalent: After Effects: incoming layer above in Lighter Color blend mode (per-pixel brighter pick, hard edges); keyframe the incoming layer's Levels/Exposure from black up to normal while the outgoing layer ramps from normal down to black, so the brighter pixel wins at every step.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (277.52-278.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows B's pale tones replacing A's dark areas within 2 frames and a near-static hard-edged mix until about +0.45 s, then B. Centred needs handles on both clips. Single-sided behaviour (against black) not verified.

verified.note: B's pale tones punch through A's dark areas from -0.3 s and the two hold as a hard-edged patchy double exposure through +0.3 s, as described.

cards.name: Page Peel (Obsolete)
cards.summary: Old version of the page-curl transition: the outgoing clip curls away from the top-left corner like a sheet of paper and the curl travels diagonally off the bottom-right, revealing the incoming clip underneath. The back of the page is a plain grey-white shaded paper, not the image. Kept only for old projects.
use_for: deliberately kitschy retro or storybook gag in a satire reel
turning a 'page' of a document or newspaper in an explainer (prefer the current Page Turn / Page Peel)
avoid: any serious documentary, news or trailer: reads as cheap 2000s wedding video
new edits: use the current Page Peel or Page Turn instead
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Page Peel or Page Turn (Page Peel folder). After Effects: CC Page Turn effect on the outgoing layer, keyframing Fold Position across the frame.
cards.scripting: Apply by the exact name including ' (Obsolete)'; do not substring-match, because the current 'Page Peel' also exists. Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (281.52-282.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) confirms the top-left to bottom-right curl with a grey paper back. Whether it is listed in the Effects panel is not confirmed (may be reachable only by name through QE).

verified.note: A curls away from the top-left corner with a grey-white shaded paper back, the curl crosses diagonally and sits at the bottom-right corner at +0.3 s, revealing B underneath.

cards.name: Radial Wipe (Legacy)
cards.summary: Older build of Radial Wipe: a hard straight edge pivots on the top-left corner and sweeps clockwise from the top edge down to the left edge, like a clock hand, revealing the incoming clip (the outgoing clip's last sliver sits in the bottom-left). Replaced by the current Radial Wipe.
use_for: countdown or 'time running out' beat in a news explainer
radar-style reveal of a map or data graphic
retro game-show style satire segment
avoid: emotional documentary moments: too mechanical
hard edge with no feather looks dated
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Radial Wipe (current). After Effects: Radial Wipe effect on the outgoing layer above the incoming one, Wipe Center at the top-left corner [0, 0], Start Angle 90 degrees, Wipe Clockwise, Transition Completion 0->25% over the duration (only one quadrant of the sweep is in frame); add a little Feather to soften.
cards.scripting: Apply by the exact name including ' (Legacy)'. Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (285.52-286.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) confirms the top-left pivot and clockwise sweep with a hard, unfeathered edge. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: Hard straight edge pivoting near the top-left corner sweeps clockwise, B above/right of it and A left in a shrinking bottom-left wedge.

cards.name: Split (Legacy)
cards.summary: Older build of Split: the outgoing clip splits along a vertical centre line and the two halves slide apart to the left and right like doors opening, revealing the incoming clip in a widening centre strip. Replaced by the current Split.
use_for: reveal of a title, logo or leader photo behind 'opening doors'
satire segment 'behind closed doors' gag
chapter opener in a political explainer
avoid: subject's face on the centre line gets cut in half during the move
overuse looks like a 2000s slideshow
cards.equivalent: Premiere replacement: Split (non-legacy). After Effects: duplicate the outgoing layer, mask left/right halves, and animate Position of each half off-frame (ease out), incoming layer below.
cards.scripting: Apply by the exact name including ' (Legacy)'. Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (289.52-290.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) confirms the vertical seam with the halves sliding horizontally. Orientation is an Effect Controls setting not settable from a spec, so the bridge gets the vertical split. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: A splits on a vertical centre seam and the halves slide left and right, B showing in a widening centre strip (~130 px at -0.3 s, ~310 px at the cut, most of frame at +0.3 s).

cards.name: VR Chroma Leaks
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) transition that blends the clips under a violent colour burn: the outgoing clip floods hot yellow-orange just before the cut, then the incoming clip emerges through magenta, blue and cyan fringes that fade away. It renders on flat footage too.
use_for: energetic social reel transitions on music beats
AI-education channel intros and section changes
trailer montage glow-through between shots
travel or event B-roll
avoid: solemn documentary, hard news or political explainers: far too loud
faces at the cut: they burn out to yellow for several frames
flat (non-360) edits where a more controllable leak is wanted: use Premiere's 'Chroma Leak' transition
cards.equivalent: Premiere flat-footage counterpart: 'Chroma Leak'. After Effects: cross-dissolve plus a colour light-leak clip on Screen or Add over the cut; or a Fractal Noise layer colourised with Colorama (yellow to magenta to cyan), blurred, on Add, with Opacity peaking at the cut.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (293.52-294.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows the frame almost fully yellow from about -0.16 s to the cut and magenta/cyan fringes on B until about +0.3 s. Leak colour and VR projection controls (Auto VR Properties) are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec, so defaults apply.

verified.note: Frame at the cut is flooded hot yellow-orange over a mix of A and B; at +0.3 s B carries magenta/blue fringes, faint cyan/pink tint on A at -0.3 s.

cards.name: VR Gradient Wipe
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) wipe meant to reveal the incoming clip along a soft gradient. With the defaults a script gets on flat footage it does not read as a wipe: the outgoing clip vanishes within about two frames of the transition start, and a few of its brightest fragments (flowers, a small gold detail) linger over the incoming clip until the end, which looks like a hard cut with leftover artefacts.
use_for: nothing in scripted flat edits; only a hand-tuned 360 project where an editor sets the gradient and softness
avoid: any scripted transition: defaults give a jump cut plus stray fragments
soft wipes in explainers: use Cross Dissolve, or Linear Wipe with feather
cards.equivalent: For the intended soft gradient wipe: After Effects Gradient Wipe effect with a Gradient Ramp layer as the map and Transition Softness ~50%, or Linear Wipe with a large Feather; in Premiere a plain Cross Dissolve.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (297.52-298.52 s) with no error, but Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows clip A gone by about -0.44 s except bright fragments that stay until about +0.5 s. The gradient and softness controls are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec, so the planner should not choose it.

verified.note: B is already full frame at -0.3 s with bright A fragments (flowers, gold swooshes) floating over it at the cut and still a few at +0.3 s: a near hard cut with artefacts, as described.

cards.name: VR Iris Wipe
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) iris: a soft-edged circle of the incoming clip opens from about the frame centre and grows until it fills the frame. On flat 16:9 footage the circle stretches into a rounded rectangle as it grows.
use_for: revealing a person or object from the centre in an explainer
playful 'spotlight' reveal in a reel
360 documentary scene changes centred on the viewer's gaze
avoid: hard-news segments: the circle feels cartoonish
subject off-centre while the iris opens at centre
cards.equivalent: Premiere flat-footage counterpart: 'Iris Round'. After Effects: an ellipse mask on the incoming layer whose Mask Expansion (or the shape's size) animates open with Mask Feather ~40 px; or the Iris Wipe effect.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (301.52-302.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows a small circle near centre at -0.24 s, a large soft rounded rectangle at the cut, and full B by about +0.3 s. Centre (pan/tilt) and feather are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec, so it always opens at the centre.

verified.note: Small circle of B at frame centre at -0.3 s, a large soft-edged rounded rectangle of B at the cut, full B at +0.3 s.

cards.name: VR Light Leaks
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) transition that washes the whole frame in shifting saturated colour: the outgoing clip tints pink-magenta, then orange and a near-white yellow burn at the cut, and the incoming clip comes out green-cyan before clearing. At defaults it is a loud rainbow wash, not a subtle warm film leak.
use_for: beat-drop transitions in party, festival or music-driven reels
high-energy AI-education channel intro or section change
deliberately trippy montage moment
avoid: documentary, hard news and political explainers: too loud and the colour shift reads as a grading error
faces at the cut: they disappear into the yellow-white burn
warm nostalgic or memory moments: use Premiere's 'Light Leak' transition or a real light-leak clip on Screen instead
cards.equivalent: Premiere flat-footage counterpart for a warm film leak: 'Light Leak'. After Effects: an adjustment layer with Colorama (or a Gradient Ramp in Color/Overlay mode) cycling magenta to yellow to cyan over the cut, plus Exposure ramping up to near-white at the cut, under a cross-dissolve.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (305.52-306.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows the tint starting about -0.36 s, near-white yellow at the cut and a green-cyan cast on B until about +0.4 s. Leak colour controls are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec, so the default rainbow look always applies. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: A tinted pink-magenta at -0.3 s, near-white yellow wash with green blotches at the cut, B with a green-cyan cast at +0.3 s.

cards.name: VR Light Rays
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) transition: a cross-dissolve with a bright star-burst of light rays that flares up from a point near the frame centre around the cut and dies away. The burst covers roughly the middle third of the frame; the rest of the image is a normal mix of the two clips.
use_for: reveal of a hero shot, leader or monument in a celebratory news reel
trailer hit into a title or logo centred in frame
AI-education 'breakthrough' or 'idea' moment
avoid: subtle documentary scenes: the sparkle looks like a cheap preset
a face at the frame centre at the cut: the burst sits right on it
cards.equivalent: After Effects: cross-dissolve plus CC Light Burst 2.5 or CC Light Rays on an adjustment layer (centre at frame centre) with Intensity keyframed 0 -> peak at the cut -> 0; a small Lens Flare at centre adds the star.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (309.52-310.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows the burst from about -0.16 s, peaking at the cut, faint streaks on B until about +0.2 s. Ray centre and intensity are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec.

verified.note: Cross-dissolve with a bright star-burst of rays at frame centre at the cut covering roughly the middle third; clean A at -0.3 s and clean B at +0.3 s.

cards.name: VR Mobius Zoom
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) zoom: the outgoing clip bends into a spherical, fish-eye wrap while the incoming clip opens from a small circle at the frame centre and grows outward, pushing the wrapped remains of the outgoing clip off the left and right edges as spheres.
use_for: high-energy reel transitions on a beat drop
'diving into' a topic in an AI-education video
trippy montage moments in a trailer or music-driven edit
avoid: faces near the edge get heavily distorted on flat footage
serious news or documentary: reads as gimmick
cards.equivalent: After Effects: zoom transition: Scale the outgoing layer up into the cut and the incoming layer down from oversize with CC Radial Fast Blur / Radial Blur (Zoom) peaking at the cut; add CC Lens or Optics Compensation for the spherical warp.
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (313.52-314.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) shows a barrel-warped A with a small B circle at -0.3 s, B in a large centre circle at the cut, warped A spheres at the edges until about +0.16 s. Single-sided behaviour not verified, set false to be safe. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: A barrel-warped with a small B circle at centre at -0.3 s, B in a large centre opening with wrapped A spheres at left and right edges at the cut, slight top-edge warp on B at +0.3 s.

cards.name: VR Random Blocks
cards.summary: Immersive Video (360) block dissolve: small rectangular blocks of the incoming clip pop in at random positions until they cover the frame; at the cut the image is a jumble of both clips, and a few stray blocks of the outgoing clip linger briefly after it. On flat footage it looks like a digital blocky dissolve.
use_for: tech / data segments in an AI-education explainer
'loading' or hacked-data beat in a news reel
glitchy reel transitions when paired with a glitch SFX
avoid: emotional or solemn moments: too mechanical
large slow blocks look like an old PowerPoint
cards.equivalent: Premiere flat-footage counterpart: 'Random Blocks'. After Effects: Block Dissolve effect on the outgoing layer (Transition Completion 0->100, small Block Width/Height, Feather 0).
cards.scripting: Harvest placed it centred for 1 s (317.52-318.52 s) with no error; Gallery (pve/gallery/tr, A=test plate A, B=test plate B) confirms random blocks of B from about -0.3 s, a mixed jumble at the cut and stray A blocks until about +0.3 s. Block size and feather are Effect Controls settings not settable from a spec. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: Small random blocks of B over A at -0.3 s, a jumble of both at the cut, a few stray A blocks on B at +0.3 s.
